abstract: We report a case of a cervical teratoma that was diagnosed prenatally. In anticipation of potential upper airway obstruction, resources were mobilized to the operating room at the time of planned cesarean section. The neonate developed respiratory distress, and her airway was secured. There was no evidence of cerebral anoxia initially, and she is currently thriving with no central or peripheral neurologic defects. As prenatal diagnosis by ultrasound becomes more refined, the otolaryngologist will play an increasing role in perinatal decision-making and anticipated emergencies at the time of delivery. Airway obstruction of various causes will be the most urgent problem.
abstract_ja: 頸部奇形腫が出生前に診断された症例を報告する。上気道閉塞の可能性を見越し、計画された帝王切開の際に手術室に必要な人員と機材を配備した。新生児は呼吸窮迫を呈し、気道を確保した。当初、脳の無酸素症の所見はなく、現在は神経学的な欠損なく順調に成長している。出生前超音波検査が精緻化するにつれ、耳鼻咽喉科医は周産期の意思決定や分娩時に予想される緊急事態への対応で、より大きな役割を担うようになるだろう。様々な原因による気道閉塞が、最も緊急性の高い問題である。
